client: Example Client A (fictional public pension fund)
note: Fictional example of an envisioned custom voting policy, captured as a questionnaire: each position states only what differs from the house; everything else inherits the house value. 'source' is the client's own wording.

positions.source: Boards should be at least two-thirds independent; half for controlled companies.
We expect an independent chair at every company.
Non-executive directors should hold no more than four listed-company mandates.
At least 40% of board members should be women, in all markets.
CEO pay above the upper quartile of peers, or above 150 times the median employee, is excessive.
Every company should link at least 20% of variable pay to sustainability targets.
Severance should not exceed one year of pay.
Non-audit fees should not exceed half of audit fees.
Issuance without pre-emption rights should be limited to 5% of capital.
We have no objection to virtual-only meetings.
Where a company scores below 30 on the CLTI and shows no progress after six months of engagement, we vote against the chair, in any sector.
All companies should have science-based, independently validated targets.
We vote against climate plans that score below 70 in the transition plan assessment.
We vote against the responsible director at nature laggards.
Serious (severity 4 and above) human-rights controversies should lead to a vote against the chair.
Escalation votes do not need to be announced to the company in advance.
We support governance proposals that strengthen shareholder rights.

unclear.source: Remuneration should be reasonable and aligned with long-term value creation.
unclear.question: Should say-on-pay follow the house red-flag approach, or do you want a stricter default (e.g. against unless all remuneration criteria are met)?

unmapped.source: We vote against the chair of companies planning new fossil-fuel expansion.
We expect companies to pay a living wage across their supply chain.
